text:
alex_w: Heads up — saw a WS connection go into a ~7s stall then resume. Console flagged route as throttled for that session even though backend logs show continuous processing. :eyes:

samir: Any traces/trace_id? Is this one of the EU shards?

alex_w: trace: trace-202603-xyz123 (attached in the trace service). EU shard. Here's the small part of the wire log:```
[12:30:01.001] RECV 24 bytes -> frame: {type: text, len: 8, payload: "."}
[12:30:01.205] RECV 8 bytes  -> frame: {type: ping}
[12:30:08.300] RECV 14 bytes -> frame: {type: text, len: 6, payload: "hi"}
```
Looks like tiny frames spaced out. Console counts this as no progress and flips to throttle policy.

mei_li: Hmm — our routing throttle uses ack latency measured at proxy TCP-level + tokens emitted metric. Small frames might not bump tokens_emitted if the app aggregates at the model runtime. So proxy sees long ack gaps and increments route penalty.

jordan: Is the proxy measuring `last_ack_ms` against `last_application_progress_ms`? I thought we normalized by `tokens_emitted` when available.

alex_w: For this path we didn't have tokens_emitted due to the older model adapter. So fallback is pure ack-based. That explains it.

samir: Can we confirm whether these tiny frames are keepalive vs payload? If keepalive, we should ignore for throttle. If payload, maybe the runtime isn't emitting tokens yet (e.g., partial KV cache wake).

alex_w: I grepped logs — payload frames had JSON like {"delta":"\u0002"} (single char deltas). Not just pings. So app-level progress is minimal.

mei_li: Proposal: change throttle heuristic to treat frames < 32 bytes as "micro-frame" and only count as progress if cumulative micro-bytes within last window exceed threshold. That avoids penalizing interactive tiny-burst streams.

jordan: Risk: attack vector — lots of micro-frames could be used to keep sockets alive and consume slots. We'd need rate limits.

samir: Alternative: prefer app-level signals when available. For older adapters, add a cheap shim that emits `progress=true` once per N bytes of payload to the proxy sidecar, then routing uses that flag. Cheaper than changing core heuristic.

alex_w: shim sounds safe. Quick patch: sidecar sets header `X-App-Progress: 1` every 64 bytes of cumulative payload or when a newline delim seen. Proxy increments progress on that header.

mei_li: Could also add console telemetry flag `last_frame_size` and `micro_frame_count` so operators can see why route was penalized. Right now console only shows `last_ack` and `tokens_emitted` which made the UX confusing.

samir: +1 to telemetry. It's low risk and helps debugging. Add to rollout as off by default.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: routing-proxy/shim-progress v1.1 -> canary host group alpha (10%). ETA 09:00 UTC.

jordan: For immediate mitigation, can we temporarily raise the ack-threshold for route penalty from 5s->12s in EU? That'll reduce false-throttles while we roll the shim.

mei_li: I'd rather not change global ack thresholds. Maybe per-route config: add `micro_frame_grace_ms` default 8000ms only on affected tenant routes. Safer and reversible.

alex_w: I can create a per-tenant flag for the tenant in question. Will test locally with the shim.

samir: Ops/console note: update the route detail page to show a stacked timeline: ack gaps (grey), micro-frame spikes (yellow), token emissions (green). That should make the behavior obvious in postmortems.

jordan: Also add a small diagnostic CLI: `ri inspect-stream --trace trace-202603-xyz123` that prints the micro-frame histogram. Would speed triage.

alex_w: Working on the shim PR and diagnostic tool. Will post link when ready. TL;DR: root cause = small payload frames + legacy adapter -> ack-only fallback -> route penalty. Fix = shim progress header + console telemetry + per-route grace config.

mei_li: Sounds good. Quick follow-ups: 1) Can you capture a few more sample traces across shards? 2) Add a test that simulates micro-frame bursts so we don't regress.

alex_w: On it. I'll add load test sim that sends 1-8 byte frames at configurable intervals.

samir: Thanks. If deploy-bot finishes canary and metrics look stable, let's schedule a slow rollout. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary started. Monitor at https://console.internal/redwood/proxy/canaries/1234 (alpha -> 10%).

jordan: Nice. Also, add a note in the runbook: "If route shows throttle but tokens_emitted>0, check micro-frame histogram". Saves future confusion.

alex_w: Will update runbook and drop the PR link here when ready. :party_parrot:
